why: Read coprimality into the statement as every source does. The exceptional-set papers (BLT v1, Bernert, Li) give power-saving counts of the conjecture's exceptional set, which move a quantity toward finiteness without settling it: bound. Lichtman's note is expository on de Bruijn's classical estimate, so none. AxiomProver's theorem assumes abc and answers a different question (variant), though by the authors' quote it was AI-generated. Whole-problem claims inside the window (Joshi IV, the Zenodo items, Carella's disproof) are set aside as not_credible: Joshi IV was the close call, since he is an established arithmetic geometer, but a reported specific error (Scholze, Prop 6.10.7), 31 months without acceptance, ongoing 'open' status in LANA and Wikipedia, and his own drift to a conditional framing together pass the F10 bar. Mochizuki 2012 is knocked down on the Scholze-Stix Corollary 3.12 gap, which the community has not accepted as answered. Carella's refutation would be whole scope (a failure for any ε refutes the universal claim) but carries many fringe signals.
doubts: Statement read literally (without gcd condition) is trivially false; judged on the coprime reading. Joshi IV credibility (not_credible vs doubtful) and Mochizuki (knocked_down vs doubtful) are judgment calls; the Scholze Prop 6.10.7 error is known only via nLab. Carella note is only 8 weeks old.
